name: Street Safety in Dujiangyan: Pairwise Comparison
description:
Method replication: participants compare 30 pairs of street views from Dujiangyan (Sichuan), each shown as four directions (front, right, back, left) in a 2 × 2 grid, and click the picture that leaves them with a safer impression, or choose Tie; the images are not the paper's stimuli (68 re-fetched Baidu street view panoramas across the city, 2016–2023).

Original study: Wang, Zeng, Li & Deng (2022), ISPRS International Journal of Geo-Information 11(9), 465. From 11,584 Baidu panoramas of Dujiangyan, a geographically even subset was built; each panorama's four views were joined in a 2 × 2 grid. On a crowdsourcing website, volunteers saw random pairs and answered "Which picture leaves you with a safer impression?" (win / loss / tie). TrueSkill and LambdaRank turned the clicks into safety scores, 15 experts then labelled 1,142 images, and a reinforcement-learning model predicted safety from segmentation-based features.

Differences from the original study: (1) newly fetched Baidu panoramas instead of the authors' images, which are not released; (2) a fixed 30 random pairs per participant instead of open-ended clicking on the website; (3) a Tie button is shown explicitly, and gender, age and familiarity with Dujiangyan are asked first; (4) the expert labelling and the prediction model are not part of the survey.
author: Wang, Zeng, Li & Deng
